This valuation gap suggests that the market has over-indexed on past revenue trends while ignoring the company's emerging ability to outperform expectations [E57]. Although the bear cites a sector sales growth of 8.0% [E76], the company’s current P/E of 13.2x [E1] provides a margin of safety that the sector’s higher valuation multiples do not offer. By focusing exclusively on the rearview mirror of sales growth, the bear misses the fundamental shift toward profitability that is currently being signaled by the scanX engine [E57].

The bull’s reliance on a 695% profit growth signal [E57] is misleading because it ignores the persistent, long-term decay in the company’s core business, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth of -14% [E14] and a 5-year decline of -12% [E15, E63]. The valuation discount to book value [E2, E7] is not a margin of safety but a rational market response to a company that has failed to keep pace with the sector’s 8.0% sales growth [E76] and currently offers shareholders a 0.00% dividend yield [E4].
